offspring.title: Randomised-override logging with doubly-robust step labels
offspring.method: Branching (C01) forks every step K times per instance: cost ~ T*2*K runs. Inspired by it and by the two-head probe (C02), collect labels from ONE trajectory per instance in which, at each step, the default call decision is overridden with probability eps (e.g. 0.3) by a coin flip (the propensity is known). Estimate Delta_t per step with a doubly-robust estimator: outcome model m(h_t, a) fitted on the logs, corrected by inverse-propensity residuals on overridden steps. Train the two-head probe (C02) on DR labels.
offspring.experiment: Compare probes trained on (i) branched labels K=3, (ii) DR labels from randomised logs at equal total number of model rollouts, (iii) naive on-policy labels (no randomisation). Metric: Delta-sign AUROC and U-AUC on held-out instances; rollouts needed to reach branched-label U-AUC.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Changes the LABEL SOURCE: replaces counterfactual forking with randomised logging + doubly-robust estimation; keeps C02's two-head probe. New claim: label cost, not estimator form, is the practical barrier.
offspring.hypothesis: At equal rollout budget, probes trained on doubly-robust labels from randomised-override logs reach a higher U-AUC than probes trained on branched labels, and exceed naive on-policy labels by a margin that disappears when eps = 0.
offspring.novelty_note: Off-policy estimation of counterfactual tool utility is not in the matrix; E11 constructs labels by running both arms for every instance.

offspring.title: Decision-flip detection between consecutive steps
offspring.method: Headroom (C01) exists only where the optimal action changes between steps given new information; the feature comparison (C12) asks what signal reveals it. Define a flip F_t = 1[sign(Delta_t - lambda*c) != sign(Delta_{t-1} - lambda*c)] using branched labels. Train a flip detector on features of the step transition: hidden-state difference (h_t - h_{t-1}), token-probability statistics of the new step, and previous tool output size/type. Use the detector (i) as an analysis tool to locate where headroom lives, and (ii) as extra input to the utility probe.
offspring.experiment: Flip rate per env and lambda; AUROC of flip detection for hidden-difference vs token-prob features; U-AUC of utility probe with and without flip features.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Moves from 'is there headroom' and 'which features' to 'when does the decision change', a different target variable (decision flips). Does not claim overhead savings (rejected P1-C05).
offspring.hypothesis: Decision flips occur on at least 15% of steps in at least one benchmark, and hidden-state-difference features detect them with AUROC at least 0.05 above token-probability features.
offspring.novelty_note: Flip-level analysis of tool necessity is absent from the matrix; relies on C01 labels.

offspring.title: Posterior expected-regret call rule with a bootstrap probe ensemble
offspring.method: Weakest criticism of C03: regret-weighted point estimates may match two-head probes and degrade with noisy labels. Change ONE component, the decision rule: train B=10 bootstrap probes on resampled steps; at each step compute the posterior over Delta_t from the ensemble and call iff E[max(0, Delta_t - lambda*c)] exceeds E[max(0, lambda*c - Delta_t)] weighted by an asymmetry factor rho (missed necessary call costs rho times an unnecessary one; rho = 1 recovers the point rule).
offspring.experiment: Label-noise sweep (0, 10, 20%) vs C03 point rule and two-head subtraction at equal training data; report per-step regret and U-AUC; B in {1,5,10}.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Only the decision rule changes (point estimate -> posterior expected regret with asymmetry rho). Loss and features unchanged.
offspring.hypothesis: At 20% label noise, the ensemble posterior rule has lower mean per-step decision regret than the point-estimate regret-weighted scorer, and the two are equal at 0% noise within a paired-bootstrap CI.
offspring.novelty_note: Ensemble uncertainty for tool decisions is not claimed novel in general; contribution is regret-aware use for step-wise calls.

offspring.title: Confidence-informed prior for adaptive-sample stopping
offspring.method: Weakest criticism of C03: flat Beta prior gives slow stopping on ambiguous queries; many queries hit the sample cap. Change ONE component, the prior: initialise the Beta posterior over p_correct from a calibrated verbalized-confidence estimate (isotonic map, E15) with a prior strength n0 (pseudo-samples) chosen on validation; sampling and stopping boundary (posterior mass vs lambda*c) unchanged.
offspring.experiment: Mean samples per query, cap-hit rate and U net of sampling cost vs flat-prior SPRT and fixed k; n0 in {1,2,4}.
offspring.hypothesis: At matched U (within 1 point), the informed prior reduces mean samples per query by at least 25% relative to a flat prior.
offspring.novelty_note: Combining verbalized priors with sequential sampling for call decisions is not in the matrix; risk: E27 says verbalized confidence is overconfident.

offspring.compatibility_check: Both are black-box, use the same labelled calibration split, and produce a direct-side estimate that feeds the same cost rule; C05's hybrid estimator can replace C01's p_direct component. No contradictory assumptions. COMPATIBLE.
offspring.title: Failure-aware two-sided benefit estimator
offspring.method: p_direct_hat = hybrid of sample agreement and calibrated verbalized confidence with a learned correction for the confidently-wrong zone (C05: agreement >= 0.8 yet wrong); p_tool_hat = per-query classifier from query features with group split (C01). Delta_hat = p_tool_hat - p_direct_hat; call iff Delta_hat > lambda*c + sampling cost.
offspring.experiment: Anchor scenarios (reduced); baselines CTA global-p_ret rule, consistency-only, verbalized-only, anchor explicit modelling (reduced). Metric U-AUC net of signal cost; ECE of Delta_hat; confidently-wrong recall.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Integrates C05's confidently-wrong correction into C01's p_direct side; keeps C01's per-query p_tool.
offspring.hypothesis: The failure-aware p_direct reduces confidently-wrong calls skipped by at least 30% relative to calibrated consistency alone, and the combined two-sided rule exceeds the CTA global-p_ret rule on U-AUC on at least 2 of 3 scenarios.

offspring.compatibility_check: Same parents, different integration: C05's confidently-wrong analysis defines WHEN the extra p_tool model is worth consulting. Requires a gate threshold on the direct-side signal, which both parents already expose. COMPATIBLE.
offspring.title: Gated per-query tool-benefit estimation
offspring.method: Stage 1: decide from direct-side signals alone when they are clearly high (answer directly) or clearly low (call). Stage 2: only in the ambiguous / confidently-wrong zone defined from C05's stratification, consult the per-query p_tool_hat of C01 and decide with Delta_hat. The gate thresholds are chosen on validation by net U.
offspring.experiment: Gate rate (share reaching stage 2), U-AUC and signal cost vs always-two-sided (P2-G1b), direct-only, and CTA.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Differs from G1b by conditional use of p_tool_hat (cost/artifact exposure reduced) rather than always applying it.
offspring.hypothesis: The gated rule attains U-AUC within 1 point of the always-two-sided rule while querying p_tool_hat for fewer than half of the queries, and its advantage over direct-only is concentrated in the gated region.
offspring.novelty_note: Gating is partly an engineering choice; claim is the evidence about where p_tool matters.
